prompt: A vertical 9:16 photograph taken from almost ground level at the kerb of a British city junction at night in steady rain, the camera just behind and below a police motorcycle outrider. His raised black leather glove, palm out, fills the upper left of the frame, large, soft and out of focus, a rim of sodium-orange light along its fingers and the shoulder of his hi-vis jacket cut by the left edge. Past the glove, sharp in the middle of the frame, a British ambulance in yellow-and-green chequered livery sits stopped at a red light, its blue beacons mid-flash, its windscreen a dark slab with two faint figures behind it, its lettering lost in glare. Across the space between the glove and the ambulance, a dark saloon car slides through the junction from right to left as a long smear of black bodywork and white headlight streak, a second one following just behind it at the right edge. The lower half of the picture is wet tarmac a few centimetres from the lens, rain spattering in a puddle that holds broken vertical reflections of red, blue and orange. One sodium street lamp blooms high in the top right through the drizzle; the sky and shadows go teal-black. Shot on CineStill 800T with a 28mm lens at a wide aperture, red halation round the red signal and the beacons, coarse grain, underexposed with lifted blacks, slightly tilted as if handheld. Thanks.
